text_blocks.snippet: A ground glass opacity (GGO) seen on a CT scan of the lungs can be a sign of lung cancer, but it can also be caused by other conditions. GGOs are hazy areas that appear on scans and can indicate early-stage lung cancer, particularly lung adenocarcinoma. However, they can also be associated with benign conditions like inflammation, fibrosis, or hemorrhage.
